rules.statement: In a GitHub Actions workflow, don't put a job that must finish (such as one that records results on close) in the same concurrency group as a job that sets `cancel-in-progress: true`; give it its own group or make sure the cancelling job can't trigger while it runs.
rules.why: `cancel-in-progress: false` on a job only controls what that job cancels, not whether other runs cancel it. A newer run in the shared group can also take the group's single pending slot and replace the queued job, so its work is silently lost and nothing retries it.
rules.check: Look for jobs that share a `concurrency.group` expression where one sets `cancel-in-progress: true` and the other is expected to always complete. Also look for triggers, such as a comment command on a closed pull request, that could start the cancelling job while the other one runs.

rules.statement: In NCodeGroup's code-review workflow, don't report that a job reads `NCODE_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` without `environment: code-review`: the key is an organization secret limited to the opted-in repositories, and the `code-review` environment holds no secrets.
rules.why: The `code-review` environment exists only so that Anthropic's federation rule trusts the review job's OIDC token. A job without the environment and without `id-token: write` can already read the key, so leaving out the environment widens nothing. Moving the key into an environment is tracked as a separate hardening task.
rules.check: Before reporting a missing `environment:` on a job that uses the review app's key, check whether the job requests `id-token: write` or needs the federated identity. Only that case calls for the `code-review` environment.

rules.statement: When a change rewords a comment that explains how a workflow or script works, such as where secrets live, update every other comment in the same file that describes the same thing so that they agree.
rules.why: Comments that contradict each other give conflicting setup and debugging instructions, and one of them is wrong.
rules.check: When a diff adds or changes an explanatory comment, look for unchanged comments elsewhere in the file, such as setup notes or headers, that still describe the old behavior.
